Config.Title: Void Taint Configuration
Config.MenuHint: Configure the threshold and consequence tables for Void Taint.
Config.Introduction: Void Taint measures in levels how deeply the Void has corrupted a creature. Its safe threshold equals Proficiency Bonus + CHA modifier, but never less than the configured minimum.
Config.MinimumThresholdHint: The calculated threshold can’t be lower than this value.
Config.TablesHint: The standard tables are ordinary world Roll Tables. Edit them directly or replace them with other Roll Tables.

Rules.Title: Standard Rules
Rules.Accruing: A creature can safely accumulate Void Taint up to its threshold. As soon as the value exceeds the threshold by at least 1, it gains an Indefinite Dread or chooses a Flesh Warp instead; its Void Taint then resets to 0.
Rules.Recovery: Outside the Void, a creature reduces its Void Taint by 1 after 1 week per current Void Taint level. Any Void Exposure save during this time restarts the recovery period.
Rules.Restoration: Greater restoration or similarly potent magic of 5th circle or higher reduces Void Taint by 1. For an Indefinite Dread caused by Void Taint, the target can then make a CHA save against DC 10 + its remaining Void Taint to end one such dread.
Rules.Regenerate: A Flesh Warp caused by Void Taint can only be removed from a willing creature by the regenerate ritual or similarly potent magic of 7th circle or higher.
Rules.Immunity: Creatures native to the Void or already suffused with the Void’s influence are immune to the effects of Void Taint.

Overview.Title: Feuerschwinge overview
Overview.Text: Feuerschwinge combines campaign tools for Black Flag in one module.
Overview.Point1: The Feuerschwinge tools bring together session management, Challenge Manager, downtime and project overviews, GM tools, Campaign & Rewards, the library, settings, and help. Available entries depend on user and world roles.
Overview.Point2: The Feuerschwinge Library exposes content from the system, module, and supported sources.
Overview.Point3: Weapon Properties, Weapon Options, and macro activities extend weapons and Items.
Overview.Point4: Session, user, and compendium transfers move content and assignments between worlds. Shops, animal offers, and campaign rewards complement primary-world management.
Overview.Point5: Permanent rules and defaults live in module configuration; current world state, corrections, and diagnostics live in GM Tools.

CreatureBuilder.Title: Feuerschwinge Creature Builder
CreatureBuilder.Text: The Creature Builder creates a Black Flag Actor with Actions, Features, and Spells from structured creature JSON.
CreatureBuilder.Point1: Open Creature Builder from the Feuerschwinge module settings; the gear in the left Feuerschwinge control group opens those settings directly.
CreatureBuilder.Point2: Use the link in the window to open Feuerschwinge Creature Creator and generate suitable Creature JSON.
CreatureBuilder.Point3: Paste the JSON into the text field or load a JSON file, then optionally select a destination Actor folder.
CreatureBuilder.Point4: Validate reports schema errors before creation; Create Creature then builds the Actor with embedded Items and Activities.
CreatureBuilder.Point5: Official Spells are embedded from enabled installed compendiums; custom Spells are built directly from the creature JSON.
CreatureBuilder.Point6: Unavailable Spells are skipped without aborting Actor creation and then listed in a persistent warning.

Weapons.Title: Weapon Properties and Weapon Options
Weapons.Text: Custom weapon properties and options are configured per world and can trigger optional mechanics.
Weapons.Point1: Every property and option requires a unique internal ID.
Weapons.Point2: Linked macros are resolved by their macro UUID and included in Session Transfer.
Weapons.Point3: Inline code remains stored in the definition and runs with the executing user's permissions.
Weapons.Point4: Changes to definitions require a world reload.

Compendiums.Title: Compendiums and library
Compendiums.Text: Library, Audit, and Folder Transfer manage available campaign content.
Compendiums.Point1: The library searches content by category, source, and search text. Spell lists and creature and Item categories provide relevant filters; open details and previews from the results.
Compendiums.Point2: Compendium Audit finds local copies and can export a recovery file before cleanup.
Compendiums.Point3: Compendium Folder Transfer in module configuration exports complete trees including subfolders, packs, pack folders, and documents.
Compendiums.Point4: Repeated imports identify previously transferred content, compare changes, and remap references. Review the preview and back up your own changes before applying an import.

Challenge.Title: Challenge Manager and Doom
Challenge.Text: Challenge Manager controls the party, Doom, and targeted roll requests.
Challenge.Point1: Open it from the Feuerschwinge group in the left canvas toolbar or from the Combat Tracker.
Challenge.Point2: PCs owned by connected players or every participant in the active session can be added to the party together.
Challenge.Point3: Doom Bank, Party, Roll Request, and the full character picker can be collapsed independently.
Challenge.Point4: Skill checks, saving throws, and plain die rolls can be posted with an optional DC, private output, and optional average.
Challenge.Point5: Advantage, Disadvantage, Extra Action, and Recharge change Doom and create styled chat cards; plus and minus adjust the bank silently.
Challenge.Point6: The checkbox below the Doom Bank adds the remaining Doom total to its chat card. Doom starts with combat and resets when combat is deleted.

Tools.Title: Challenge Manager and pause
Tools.Text: Challenge Manager controls the party, Doom, and roll requests. Automatic unpausing keeps a world locally playable when no GM is connected.

Links.Title: Character links
Links.Text: The link tools check PCs for outdated or invalid sources.
Links.Point1: The audit changes nothing and exports a detailed report.
Links.Point2: Repairs only operate on PCs in the current world.
Links.Point3: Unambiguous Items are restored from their original source.
Links.Point4: A recovery file is exported automatically before every repair.

Campaign.Title: Campaign and rewards
Campaign.Text: In the primary world, manage Westmarches source data, player assignments, and GM and server team reward balances. Recording a reward and redeeming it for a character are separate steps.
Campaign.Point1: Open Campaign & Rewards from the Feuerschwinge tools or module settings. Full GMs manage imports, rules, and bookings; players see their assigned balances. Management is unavailable in session worlds.
Campaign.Point2: Under Data validation & import, load campaign.json from the standalone Westmarches exporter, review the preview, and import it. This updates source data without granting character milestones or reward balances.
Campaign.Point3: Assign person names and Foundry users under Player assignments, then link Actors under Characters. Unambiguous matches can be detected automatically; ambiguous matches require review. Characters are listed alphabetically.
Campaign.Point4: Under Rewards, select the person and target character. The table shows only balances with rewards remaining. A GM can redeem on behalf of another person for one of that person’s characters.
Campaign.Point5: Session-linked rewards grant one milestone and the full current session reward for the character’s level before redemption. Custom reward contents are stored with the claim.
Campaign.Point6: Redemption history remains below the open balances, including the target character, source, and requesting user. Interrupted rewards remain reserved; a GM must inspect the character and resolve the recorded steps.
Campaign.Point7: Correct balance adjusts the total claim and historical usage with a reason. Already used outside the module records usage only and grants nothing; missing milestone evidence must be assigned separately on the character.

Settlements.Title: GM and server team settlements
Settlements.Text: Sessions & settlement separates historical review from new bookings and prevents booking the same source again.
Settlements.Point1: Completing a session in the primary world automatically records a reward for the selected, assigned GM using the applicable rule. New sessions preselect the current user. Missing assignments are reported.
Settlements.Point2: Historical Westmarches sessions are not booked automatically. Use Review and book GM reward and record rewards already used outside the module so they do not become available again.
Settlements.Point3: Sessions that had ended when exported count as played; cancelled and explicitly excluded sessions do not count. Registration does not prove character attendance. New or rescheduled sessions require a fresh export.
Settlements.Point4: Link Foundry sessions to Westmarches shows the complete structured history. Assign GMs first, review title suggestions, and save matching session pairs. This associates existing evidence and claims with the same session.
Settlements.Point5: Save the active server team under Player assignments. For a weekly booking, adjust recipients to the members who were active at that time. A week can only be booked after it ends.
Settlements.Point6: The default counts weeks with at least one played guild session. Weeks run Monday through Sunday and belong to the month containing their Sunday. The default model grants no balance without an active week.
Settlements.Point7: Weekly and monthly bookings cannot both be used for the same month. Rule versions apply from their effective date; monthly calculations use the rule effective on the first day. Verify historical rules and recipients before booking past rewards.

Milestones.Title: Milestones and evidence
Milestones.Text: The milestone editor records the source, evidence, note, and optional week for each existing milestone.
Milestones.Point1: Open Milestones in the GM tools or use Assign under Campaign → Characters. Source displays the recorded entries without granting another reward.
Milestones.Point2: Choose Session, GM, Server team, Starting balance, or Correction. Manual corrections require a reason. You can document existing milestones without increasing their count.
Milestones.Point3: Evidence includes matching Foundry sessions, Westmarches registrations requiring review, and rewards actually redeemed for this character. Historical usage without a target character cannot be linked automatically.
Milestones.Point4: Reconcile milestone evidence replaces only empty, unresolved starting entries after confirmation. Verify actual attendance yourself. At most one session may be assigned per milestone week.
Milestones.Point5: Evidence can only be used up to its documented capacity. Already assigned sessions and fully used evidence cannot be duplicated.
Milestones.Point6: Rows can be edited, reordered, added, or removed. Save character applies the changes; changing the number of rows changes the milestone total. Do not add a milestone merely to label an existing one.

Commerce.Title: Shops and purchase rules
Commerce.Text: Shops use the selected character’s money. GMs manage stock, prices, access requirements, and local purchase rules.
Commerce.Point1: Configure an Actor as a merchant and drop Items or Spells into shop management. Spells become Spell Scroll offers. Adjust each offer’s price, discount, stock, visibility, and quantity per price unit.
Commerce.Point2: Shop access and purchase eligibility are separate. Minimum level, languages, Proficiencies, a required Item, character selection, and optional token range restrict access. A configured denial message takes priority over the technical default message.
Commerce.Point3: Global rarity rules set the minimum purchase level. Items above the allowed level remain visible and can be inspected; the purchase button is disabled with a Purchase from level X hint.
Commerce.Point4: Use the lock button Purchase rules and release to give an offer its own minimum level. Leave it empty to use the rarity rule; a custom value replaces that rule for this offer only.
Commerce.Point5: Lock purchase until manually released keeps an offer visible but prevents purchases at every level. Your note replaces the level hint. Remove the lock to release it; the configured minimum level then applies again.
Commerce.Point6: Local purchase rules apply to normal Items, Spell Scrolls, and animal offers. Hidden offers remain hidden from players. Zero stock is shown only when the corresponding shop option is enabled.
Commerce.Point7: Switch to the selling tab to sell Items. A merchant can be configured to sell only; infinite stock, infinite money, and treatment of purchased Items are separate settings. Player transactions require a connected GM or the designated service user.

Animals.Title: Selling animals in shops
Animals.Text: Animal offers create independent Actors when purchased. The template remains unchanged.
Animals.Point1: Drop an NPC Actor template from the world or a compendium into shop management and enter the price per animal in gp. The offer appears under Animals.
Animals.Point2: Configure stock, discounts, visibility, and purchase rules on the offer. The template document must still be available when it is purchased.
Animals.Point3: The selected character pays. Each purchased animal becomes a separate copy in the character’s Actor folder; the player can then organize it manually.
Animals.Point4: The associated players receive ownership. Public permissions and unrelated template owners are not copied. The purchasing character must have at least one associated player.
Animals.Point5: The animal retains its data, Items, and token appearance. Its token links to the new Actor; purchasing does not place a token on a scene.
Animals.Point6: If a purchase fails, completed steps are rolled back where possible. If the module reports an incomplete rollback, a GM must check animals, money, and stock before retrying.

UserTransfer.Title: Transferring users between worlds
UserTransfer.Text: User transfer adds accounts and assignments to character and session transfers. It does not transfer character documents or reward balances.
UserTransfer.Point1: Open Import / export users from Player assignments or the module settings. The full GM role is required.
UserTransfer.Point2: Select users for export. The file includes profiles, roles, selected characters, explicit character permissions, and campaign person assignments.
UserTransfer.Point3: During import, assign each source user to an existing account, Create new, or Skip. Review name suggestions and character assignments before confirming.
UserTransfer.Point4: Existing users retain their roles and credentials. New users receive the displayed role and need a password set in Foundry afterwards. Passwords, special permissions, and macro hotbars are not transferred.
UserTransfer.Point5: Missing characters can be skipped. Import the same user export again after transferring those characters to add permissions and assignments.
UserTransfer.Point6: New session packages include the associated users. The import preview maps their IDs to target users; returning characters retain their existing primary-world owners. Cleaning up a session does not delete users.

Concentration.Title: Concentration and summons
Concentration.Text: Optional automation supports Concentration and the organization of summoned Actors.
Concentration.Point1: Enable automatic Concentration in the module settings. Active bf-qol Concentration automation is respected so both do not handle the same task at once.
Concentration.Point2: A Concentration Spell receives a marker. Damage creates a chat card with a Saving Throw and DC; the result records whether Concentration is maintained.
Concentration.Point3: Ending Concentration removes linked Active Effects. Existing or differently created Effects without that link may require manual review.
Concentration.Point4: Summoned copies are organized in an appropriate subfolder ending in Summons. The module uses the summoning character and its owners for assignment.

Trade.Title: Auctions, trade requests, and direct trading
Trade.Text: Alongside shops, the trade interface offers auctions, requests, and direct trades between characters.
Trade.Point1: In the auction house, select an Item you own, quantity, starting price, optional buyout, and duration. Listed Items are reserved for the auction; you cannot bid on your own listing.
Trade.Point2: Bids must meet the displayed minimum. Outbid users receive their previous bid back. Buyouts and settled auctions transfer the Item and payment; withdrawing an auction returns the Item and any existing bid.
Trade.Point3: A trade request specifies a wanted Item and payment in your own Items and optional gold. Payment remains reserved until the request is fulfilled or withdrawn.
Trade.Point4: In direct trading, each party selects a character and offers owned Items or money. Changes synchronize in the trade window; both parties must confirm the current offer before the exchange occurs.
Trade.Point5: Before confirming, check the selected character, quantities, and money amounts. Trades require a connected GM or the designated service user.

Help.Title: Feuerschwinge – Introduction and Help
Help.Heading: Introduction and help
Help.Introduction: This page explains the complete workflows for Game Masters and players. Each section can also be used independently as a reference.
Help.SettingHint: Explains setup, stations, projects, rewards, sessions, and downtime distribution.

QuickStart.Title: Quick start: Set up a downtime station
QuickStart.Text: The shortest path from an empty world to a usable downtime station with a project.
QuickStart.Point1: Configure a project base Item in Feuerschwinge Configuration. This ordinary Item is copied for every new project and supplies its Item type and system data; downtime rules are then added in the project editor.
QuickStart.Point2: Import a station preset or turn an Actor into a downtime station through its header. Configure its name, categories, progress, and checks.
QuickStart.Point3: Then create a blank project or project template directly under the station's Public Projects. A project created there is assigned to the station automatically when saved.
QuickStart.Point4: Configure its target, prerequisites, and costs, and add at least one Item or character reward. The optional default cost Item provides quick access to a frequently used cost.
QuickStart.Point5: Grant downtime through the Downtime Overview or session rewards.
QuickStart.Point6: Players open the station through its token or Actor, start a project, and invest their downtime. To open the station as a user, a GM selects that user's character token, holds Shift, and then opens the station.

Downtime.Title: Downtime balance
Downtime.Text: Downtime is a numeric value on each character and the module's central resource.
Downtime.Point1: Every character has an individual balance stored directly in an Actor flag.
Downtime.Point2: Investments and paid completion-check retries deduct downtime immediately.
Downtime.Point3: Downtime can come from direct grants, sessions, passive grants, or redeemable downtime Items.
Downtime.Point4: Cancelling a project does not automatically refund spent downtime or materials.

Stations.Title: Downtime stations
Stations.Text: Stations determine how characters create progress and which projects are available.
Stations.Point1: A GM can import a built-in station preset or turn any Actor into a station using the hammer control in its header.
Stations.Point2: Enabled controls current availability; display name and description are shown to users.
Stations.Point3: Base progress, progress sources, and additional modifiers form the progress formula.
Stations.Point4: Required checks, roll interval, allowed checks, and result table generally apply to every station project.
Stations.Point5: An optional station tool can be required; the module checks the character's ownership and Expertise.
Stations.Point6: Public projects are always allowed. Personal inventory projects require at least one category selected in the station configuration.

Projects.Title: Projects and recipes
Projects.Text: Projects define the target, requirements, costs, and result of a downtime activity.
Projects.Point1: New projects copy the configured project base Item and are stored in the Downtime Projects Item folder.
Projects.Point2: Required total progress sets the target; Repeatable resets progress after successful completion.
Projects.Point3: Required Items are consumed once at project start. Required tools are checked but not consumed.
Projects.Point4: Completion costs are consumed only immediately before rewards are granted successfully.
Projects.Point5: At least one Item or character reward is required. An Item quantity of 0 lets the result table determine its quantity.
Projects.Point6: A project result table overrides the station table for that project.
Projects.Point7: Projects can be disabled or cancelled through the Downtime Overview or station; spent resources remain spent.
Projects.Point8: Character rewards can grant languages, Proficiencies, and other supported character traits.
Projects.Point9: Collaborative projects have a project leader; other participants can join and contribute their own downtime to shared progress.

Templates.Title: Project and station presets
Templates.Text: Presets provide editable starting points, not immutable special rules.
Templates.Point1: Project templates can be created centrally in the Project Library or directly under a station's Public Projects.
Templates.Point2: Crafting, Research, Work, Training, Carousing, and Recovery provide suitable names, images, descriptions, and base values.
Templates.Point3: The project Item is created only on Save. Closing discards the draft; creation inside a station assigns the saved project automatically.
Templates.Point4: World-specific rewards, materials, costs, and tools must be added through drag and drop before saving.
Templates.Point5: Station presets create freely editable Actors in the Downtime Station Actor folder and can optionally create a matching project draft.
Templates.Point6: Work, research, training, and carousing station presets follow the intended downtime rules and remain fully editable after import.

Progress.Title: Progress calculation
Progress.Text: A station calculates progress from downtime, sources, modifiers, roll results, and an optional character value.
Progress.Point1: Base value applies per invested downtime and forms the starting point.
Progress.Point2: Character level, general Proficiency Bonus, and Expertise can be enabled and multiplied separately.
Progress.Point3: Additional modifiers add to or multiply progress and do not alter rewards.
Progress.Point4: Result tables can add to or multiply progress and reward quantity separately.
Progress.Point5: An optional character value such as reputation can be stored for this station only or shared by a selected station category.
Progress.Point6: The formula preview shows the formula and included example values before use.

Checks.Title: Checks and result tables
Checks.Text: Available checks and roll methods are taken directly from Black Flag.
Checks.Point1: Require a check requests one selected allowed check after each completed roll interval.
Checks.Point2: The table can evaluate either the natural d20 result or the full total.
Checks.Point3: Natural 1 and 20 have optional fixed rows; otherwise configured numeric ranges apply.
Checks.Point4: A pending check blocks further investment until it is rolled and resolved.
Checks.Point5: A selected competency's Proficiency / Expertise contribution can be used as a progress source independently of a check.

Completion.Title: Completion checks
Completion.Text: A project can require a successful check against a DC after reaching its progress target.
Completion.Point1: Enable the completion check with its DC and retry cost in the project's Completion section.
Completion.Point2: After reaching the target, progress remains and the project waits for the check.
Completion.Point3: The first attempt is free; only attempts after a failure cost the configured downtime.
Completion.Point4: All failures behave equally: no rewards, no completion costs, and no progress loss.
Completion.Point5: Only success consumes completion costs, grants rewards, and completes or resets the project.

Dashboard.Title: Downtime overview
Dashboard.Text: The Downtime Overview is the central GM view for active projects and direct downtime.
Dashboard.Point1: Open the Feuerschwinge control group at the bottom of the left canvas toolbar, directly below Journal Notes, then choose Downtime Overview. No token selection is required.
Dashboard.Point2: Project overview and downtime management are separate views. The project overview shows character, station, project, progress, and status; filters and collapsible sections help with large lists.
Dashboard.Point3: The Project Library and Station Presets are directly available through the buttons at the top of the Downtime Overview.
Dashboard.Point4: The row delete button only cancels that character's progress; permanent project deletion happens in the library.
Dashboard.Point5: Under Direct Downtime, a GM can grant a flat amount to selected or all included PCs; the last global grant remains visible.
Dashboard.Point6: The separate Actor Folders for Player Selection module-setting entry controls which PCs appear; all subfolders are included automatically.

Sessions.Title: Session manager
Sessions.Text: Session Manager connects preparation, world transfer, return, and subsequent reward distribution in the primary world.
Sessions.Point1: Open Session Manager from the scroll icon in the Feuerschwinge toolbar group or from the Downtime Overview; no token selection is required.
Sessions.Point2: In the primary world, prepare the session title, GM, summary, and participants. New sessions preselect the current user as GM; this can be changed. Select participants by character or player and search by name or folder.
Sessions.Point3: All, None, connected players, and controlled tokens provide quick selection. The configured Actor root limits available PCs and includes all descendants.
Sessions.Point4: Create Session Package sits beside the title. Before download, a dialog confirms participants and complete companion folders; required Macros and optionally selected compendiums travel in the package.
Sessions.Point5: The general result import remains permanently available in the primary world and identifies the returning session by its own ID rather than the last package created.
Sessions.Point6: Result import updates existing primary-world characters differentially. Completely missing characters are recreated from the complete result data in the configured Actor root. Gold multiplier, reward columns, and milestone distribution are selected afterward.
Sessions.Point7: Session rewards consist of droppable Items per character level. The gold multiplier sits in the header of rewards to distribute.
Sessions.Point8: Payout requires confirmation and uses a lock against concurrent awards. Structured history records participants and milestones. The primary world also records the assigned GM’s reward claim; redeem it later in Campaign & Rewards.
Sessions.Point9: After exporting a package, a new session can be prepared in the primary world while other sessions run concurrently in session worlds.
Sessions.Point10: When importing a package, the session world creates a top-level Actor folder named after the session. Each session character receives a separate folder inside it, with that character's companions grouped in an Extras subfolder.
Sessions.Point11: Delete Imported Session Content removes only those characters, companions, and Actor folders; Macros and compendiums remain. New Session resets session state only.

Passive.Title: Passive and direct downtime
Passive.Text: Passive downtime compensates for missed sessions; direct downtime is an immediate GM grant.
Passive.Point1: Passive downtime is configured in Session Rewards and can use weekly or monthly periods.
Passive.Point2: Rate and cap are based on configured downtime-Item rewards for the character's level.
Passive.Point3: Unselected characters accumulate passive downtime for a missed session up to the period cap.
Passive.Point4: Period settlement transfers accumulated passive downtime to the normal balance.
Passive.Point5: Direct downtime in the dashboard is a flat amount independent of level, session rewards, and percentages.

DowntimeItems.Title: Redeemable downtime Items
DowntimeItems.Text: An Item can be marked so that native use grants downtime to its owning character or displays the current balance.
DowntimeItems.Point1: Open the Item, choose Configure Downtime in its header, then Redeemable Downtime.
DowntimeItems.Point2: Set the granted amount; the module-managed description on the Item updates automatically.
DowntimeItems.Point3: In supported systems, native Item use is the main path and the system handles consumption.
DowntimeItems.Point4: Where no native hook exists, the module's fallback redemption can be used.
DowntimeItems.Point5: An Item can be either a downtime project or a redeemable downtime Item, not both at once.
DowntimeItems.Point6: An amount of 0 does not grant downtime; it displays the character's current downtime balance.

Settings.Title: Module settings
Settings.Text: Module configuration contains permanent rules, defaults, and feature switches; current world state and repairs belong in GM Tools.
Settings.Point1: Feuerschwinge configuration manages the base project Item, default cost Item, categories, milestone catch-up, and minimum levels by Item rarity. Local purchase rules are configured on each shop offer.
Settings.Point2: World role, session history, passive downtime, permanent session rewards, integrations, and automation options are configuration as well.
Settings.Point3: The default cost Item can be added to project costs with one click; Black Flag defaults to its gold Item.
Settings.Point4: The category catalog defines the categories available to stations and projects.
Settings.Point5: Actor Folders for Player Selection is a separate configuration entry; with no selection, all PCs appear.
Settings.Point6: A selected root folder limits session management and direct downtime and automatically includes every subfolder.
Settings.Point7: Project Library and Station Presets open from the Downtime Overview; Session Manager, GM Tools, Library, and Help live in the Feuerschwinge canvas controls.
Settings.Point8: Current milestone leaders, character corrections, session state, diagnostics, and technical data maintenance deliberately live in GM Tools, fully available in both primary and session worlds.

Troubleshooting.Title: Troubleshooting
Troubleshooting.Text: Most problems come from missing documents, permissions, or an older module build still being loaded.
Troubleshooting.Point1: If project creation fails, first configure a valid project base Item in Module Settings.
Troubleshooting.Point2: If a project cannot start, check rewards, materials, tools, Actor ownership, and available downtime.
Troubleshooting.Point3: If no check appears, verify Require a check and the checks allowed by that station.
Troubleshooting.Point4: If a reward is missing or an animal offer cannot be purchased, check the source Items or Actor template. For locked shop offers, also check the minimum level, manual release, and note.
Troubleshooting.Point5: Fully reload all connected clients after module updates; use Ctrl+F5 for module import/export errors in the browser console. A missing JavaScript export can indicate mixed old and new cached files.
Troubleshooting.Point6: If a session world is stuck in Ready to Play or Result Exported without imported Actors, use Delete Imported Session Content or the state-only New Session reset.
Troubleshooting.Point7: Result files are loaded through the permanently visible general result import in the primary world; another currently open session does not block them.
Troubleshooting.Point8: The browser console shows technical errors. Record the error, action, Actor, station, session, and transfer file for a reproducible report.
